title: Check yourself: Sizing a workload: limits, tiers and the bill

blocks.text: Questions on what this page has just taught. Choose one answer for each.

questions.stem: Scenario: Wicker Foods' service peaks at 600 requests a minute, each with 4,000 uncached input tokens and 300 output tokens, with 30 percent headroom. Using the tiers on the page, which is the smallest that fits?

options.text: Start, since 780 requests a minute is below its request ceiling
options.says: Ruled out because "the workload fits a tier only if all three fit".

options.text: Scale, since the headroom pushes the totals past the limits of the tier below
options.says: Ruled out because the headroom is already in the figures: "each multiplied by a headroom for peaks and growth".

options.text: A custom arrangement, since four thousand tokens a request is more than any tier allows
options.says: Ruled out because "a workload above Scale needs a custom arrangement", and this one is far below it.

options.text: Build, since only the intake volume exceeds Start's allowance while the rest fit
options.says: The three figures are 780 RPM, 3,120,000 ITPM and 234,000 OTPM, and the input figure is over Start's 2 million and under Build's 5 million.

origin.section: Three limits, and the one that binds

questions.stem: Scenario: Fjord Media's support assistant costs $38,800.00 a month without caching and $17,400.00 with it, on 2 million requests. About what share of the uncached bill does caching remove?

options.says: Ruled out because 15 percent is the batching figure: "takes a further 15 percent off by moving the share of work that can wait".
Ruled out because 30 percent is the share sent through the Batch API: "30 percent of requests through the Batch API".
The difference is $21,400.00, which is about 55 percent of $38,800.00.
Ruled out because caching removes a little over half, "because the long stable prefix is read at a tenth of the input price" and the output and the first writes are still billed.

origin.section: The bill is the same mix at different prices
